tagline: Lancaster's road down the Gorge, one waterfall after another.
intro: Out of Troutdale the old highway follows the Sandy River a few miles, then climbs past orchards and blueberry fields through Springdale and Corbett to the rim of the Columbia River Gorge. From Crown Point it comes down 600 feet on figure-eight loops into a run of waterfalls, Multnomah among them at 620 feet.

Past Dodson the old road gives way to I-84 through Hood River, and it takes up again at Mosier, where the wet western gorge turns to dry plateau, and runs on to The Dalles. Its engineer, Samuel Lancaster, began it in 1913 and said he did not want to mar what God had put there.
season: Spring for the waterfalls, fall for the weather.

moments.title: Vista House, Crown Point
moments.text: An octagonal stone rest stop 733 feet above the river, finished in 1918 with a marble interior that had some Oregonians calling it the $100,000 Outhouse.

moments.title: Horsetail Falls
moments.text: Horsetail Creek comes down the basalt right beside the road, close enough, the state's guide says, to mist your windows.

moments.title: Rowena Loops
moments.text: East of Mosier, on the dry side of the gorge, the highway climbs a stack of horseshoe curves from Rowena to the overlook on Rowena Crest.

practical: The old highway is narrow and winding, and winter storms can make it hazardous. Between Dodson and Mosier the byway runs on I-84, and just west of Mosier the restored Twin Tunnels are walked on the Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail rather than driven.
